questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I have been interested in korean music and film industry for around 5 years and have since then wanted to experience korean culture myself. 
Thus, I knew I wanted to go on exchange to Korea since I started university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It is difficult to give an overall rating of my exchange to Korea. 
On one hand it was fun to live out a dream and learn a lot of independence skills I would have never gotten staying in a secure setting in Denmark.
On the other hand there was a lot more challenges than i had anticipated. I do not regret going on exchange, but it was not as grand and amazing as I know others say it is. 
However, for me personally it was still better than staying in Denmark, as I believe the growth you have during the new and challenging times alone in a foreign country are super valuable in the long run, even though they are not always as fun in the moment.

During my exchange it was not the best, but what I have gotten with me of personal growth back home are undeniably worth the hardships.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
SNU OIA is a great site for information.

I found it a little difficult to really feel prepared for my exchange and the logistics.
I spend hours and days searching everything I could, but a lot of things you cannot figure out until you land and experience it for yourself in Korea.

The university is not so great at sending information, so do not expect to feel like you are prepared and confident in what, where, when and how of basically anything related to school.

When arriving at Incheon airport you need to go through a immigration check which I recommend reading up on before going to korea. Also SIM-cards in korea and transport from the airport to Seoul was a challenge to manage with the jetlag so maybe prepare is from home if possible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I arrived a little over a week before semester start so I had a bit of time to explore the northern parts of Seoul before going to SNU. 

The weekend before semester start there was an introduction for exchange students. The usual conference room was however under reconstruction and the new room did not have room for everyone. Instead you had to apply based on first come first served(you will learn that they love first come first served)

Also, the courses I had gave zero information before semester start. Nothing about books, what to read, what to expect anything. The only thing you get is the little description of the course and if you are lucky an overview of what each week focus on(but they do not necessarily follow their own schedule)

The Alien Registration Card you need in korea is managed by the school, but the process takes super long(it was okay for me as I didn't need it for anything). The deadlines and process is not so strict. When applying you need documentation for a living-space in Korea. It says you need proof of at least 60 days of staying there, but it can be shorter. Also if you move to another place, it is easy to change, so there is no reason to worry too much about it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
If you love and thrive in structured and well informed environments I cannot recommend SNU. 
It is possible to manage okay when you are there, but I always felt that I was under-informed and confused about why there was no information/information very late.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I wanted to live at campus, but I had a very high waiting list number. 

Luckily, there are a lot of cheap places to rent around campus. But be aware that the places can be absolutely horrible. 
Sadly, I ended up in a not so great place called THG house. I can not recommend it and everyone I know who lived there had problems with the landlord.

The one good thing about where I lived was the placement. I lived at Sillim-dong which is a more quiet area than Seoul national university station. So I can recommend living in the Sillim-dong area.

I did not want to spend too much money on rent but if I could go back and change one thing it would be finding a nicer/more pricey place.
I wish that I had used "checkmate" managed by SNU students. They help you with finding a good apartment that won't cause you unnecessary problems. It cost a bit, but it would have been worth it for me.

I also heard good things about "avengers sharehouse". I met two Danish students living there and they really liked it.

And I also heard that the dorms were fine(especially because of how cheap they are).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
You are in a bit of a risk when you rent a place on your own. I only had to pay for a few things when I moved out so I got most of my deposit back(6000kr). 

Also, some places do not have good enough plumbing for toilet paper... So you might need a trash can for toilet paper.
Just be very cautious when you go out and look at places, ask a lot of questions, and once again I recommend getting help from checkmate.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The most important is to figure out if you can live with others or need some space for yourself. If you can manage to live with others I recommend the dorms, or a sharehouse like avengers sharehouse.
(To be accepted to the dorms you need a health certificate. You can't get one in Denmark, but when you go to Korea you can apply for a health checkup with blood test, X-ray, urine test and a body scan for free)

If you want to live alone really think about how you will find a place that won't drive you insane. Like getting help from "checkmate".

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I read that a lot of people found it difficult because the courses are gone fast(first-come first-served), and you have to apply in the middle of the night(if you are still in Denmark).

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
There is a guide. It is a little confusing though.
Before the real course registration there is a trial run, where it is just for fun?? maybe to see how many want each course?

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A guide sent by mail a week or so before the trial run

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I got all the classes I wanted. 
The difficult part was making sure no classes were overlapping. Sadly I had a few classes that I really wanted but overlapped so I had to choose which I wanted most.
The courses I wanted were not that sought after, so there was no need to worry if they were gonna be full.
On top of that A LOT of students drop the courses after the semester begin(one of my classes was almost halved in participants after 3 weeks of the course)

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress too much about the courses. they are not the important part of the exchange in my opinion. 
Try to get courses with foreign teachers. I know it might sound crazy, but the worst courses I had were taught by korean teachers.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I'm sorry, but the teaching was the worst I have ever had.

Everyone I talked with who were STEM students said the teaching was kinda horrible
But I did hear that people taking humanities business and courses outside of STEM thought the classes were okay.
So maybe SNU is just not a good place for international STEM students?

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level was weird. It was both crazy difficult and way too easy. No middle ground.
I only took BA courses because I thought i was not allowed to take MA classes. In hindsight I would have probably liked to try a MA class to see if they were better?
Other students I knew who took master classes(and bachelor) said the master classes were really difficult, but also not so difficult.

Even thought I had some classes that were really difficult, it is super easy to pass. You just have to show up to class and turn in assignments and then you will pass(though it won't be the best grade, but it does not matter, as the grade is not transferred to CPH)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I much prefer the teaching at UCPH. 

If you are unlucky you might get a teacher who speaks korean when they feel like it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Biochemistry 2
2. Introduction to Chemical biology
3. Animal immunology
4. Interdisciplinary seminar in natural sciences
5. Plant cell biology

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Honestly none of them.

Biochemistry 2: Consisted of going through "lehninger principles of biochemistry" from chapter 13-22

Introduction to Chemical biology: Was way too difficult as I am so bad at chemistry. If you like hardcore chemistry it might be okay??

Animal immunology: Just no. The teacher was so unorganized, read off of slides, and often wasn't even there so it was over video instead + he did not give feedback on assignments or midterms

Interdisciplinary seminar in natural sciences: It was the least bad out of all the courses

Plant cell biology: Pretty easy but boring. Recommend it if you want to get easy through a course

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
All in all I spend 50.000KR for my total exchange(inclusive plane ticket to and from, and everything that had to do with the exchange ex. Vaccination)

+ I ended up staying at a hotel 4 different times during my stay in korea.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Nothing

(Food was more expensive than anticipated, but I also ate out at every meal)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I mostly spend time on my own. I did not join any clubs and I was not to a lot of the buddy activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I am unsure. Heard some people joined fencing clubs. 
The buddy program is nice. Planned lunch and dinner every to every other week and a lot of activities during the months

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Obviously the buddy program. Though I didn't use it much there were good times like hiking, water parks and other group activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go see the nature. That is the best part of Korea. They have beautiful mountains and excellent walking routes both crazy scary ones and beautiful relaxing ones. 
I liked the war memorial museum, olympic park and Seoul Trail.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't socialize much. Probably try to attend as many activities as you can. If you are extroverted and talkative they will open up. I you don't talk you will not befriend anyone.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
People can insist on talking korean to you even when you don't understand, and random people might approach you and insist on following you around.

The air in Korea is really polluted. If you have asthma be aware and I also had so much trouble with my eyes because of the air. They became red and hurt like crazy after days with high pollution which is almost everyday in summer and early fall.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Love that many restaurants have screens to order from and that it is not uncommon to be by yourself at cafes, restaurants ect.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not expect to learn anything school related on exchange(and I recommend to do minimal school work, attending classes is obligatory but otherwise don't focus on it, see the city instead)

Do what you really like doing. Don't go to the events if you want to explore something by yourself. And don't sit on your hands waiting for something to happen. Reach out and try new things if you want to. This exchange is for yourself, so do what you want with it.

Really be happy about and cherish the good parts. It is only four months. This also counts for when it is going bad, it is only four months and the bad things will eventually become great for personal growth

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The exchange coordinator is bad at replying to your questions. I advice to make a group chat with the people going to the same university and get to know each other and help each other along the way.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have really come to appreciate Denmark and UCPH. Nothing makes you miss and love home as going far away.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Feeling lost in my studies. I have never felt less happy or unmotivated about studying in my life

My Living situation. No heat, difficult landlord

A lot of alone time, and times where you question everything, you might feel lost and alone(but it's natural and come and pass from time to time everywhere you go.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
